history.dynasty: Yadava of Devagiri (Hemadpanthi architecture); repaired by Rani Ahilyabai Holkar
history.period: Ancient (legend attributes original to the Pandavas); present structure Yadava-era
history.summary: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, counted as the 8th and called the Adya (first) Jyotirlinga. Legend attributes the original temple to Yudhishthira during the Pandavas' exile; the Koti Rudra Samhita of the Shiva Purana places the Naganatha Jyotirlinga in Darukavana (the forest of the demon Daruka and his wife Daruki, devotee Supriya legend). The present temple is Hemadpanthi architecture in black basalt, rebuilt by the Yadavas of Devagiri, with exquisite carvings. It is said to have survived an attempted demolition by Aurangzeb when a swarm of bees attacked his men, and was later repaired by Rani Ahilyabai Holkar. Legends associate the shrine with saints Namdev, Visoba Khechara, and Dnyaneshwar — the temple is said to have turned so that Nandi sits behind the linga (unlike other Shiva temples), and unusually the temple faces west.

name: Nagnath (Nageshwar) Jyotirlinga Temple
town_description: Aundha Nagnath is a temple town in Hingoli district in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, about 64 km from the district headquarters at Hingoli. It is one of the five Jyotirlinga sites in Maharashtra and draws large pilgrim crowds, especially during Mahashivratri, Dussehra, and the Shravan month. The town lies on road and bus routes connecting Nanded, Parbhani, and Hingoli.

travel.road: Well connected by Maharashtra State Transport (MSRTC) buses from Nanded, Parbhani, and Hingoli

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Shravan month and Mahashivratri for festivals (expect large crowds)
